newsitem.title: CANADA: Air Canada says turnaround in progress.
newsitem.headline: Air Canada says turnaround in progress.

text.p: September likely marked the first month in several that Air Canada cargo revenues exceeded budget targets, says cargo chief Robert Thomson.
Preliminary indications are that September revenues exceeded plan by up to three percent, he told Reuters.
The airline's 1996 budget was set before the first-half slump in many global air freight markets. As a result, the carrier had missed its monthly revenue targets through August, Thomson said.
Like most carriers, Air Canada was forced into discounting on both North Atlantic and transpacific corridors since late-winter.
That discounting, so prevalent through the spring and summer, should dry up through the fourth quarter, said Thomson.
He said Air Canada may adjust rates during the quarter ex-Canada to Hong Kong and Seoul, but otherwise won't look at raising rates until early next year.
"Our biggest weakness was on the Atlantic, mainly outbound (from) Europe, and we are starting to see it pick up nicely," he said.
"We haven't been doing too badly in terms of Canada to Europe.

Thomson said Air Canada's North Atlantic cargo traffic was up 6.5 percent in September over August, and October traffic is expected to rise by a further 13-14 percent over September levels - indicative of a respectable fourth quarter peak.
Pacific volumes remained decent throughout the slump, but ex-Asia yields fell by about 20 percent, said Thomson.
The airline's ex-India market also took a hit, as both yields and traffic plummeted due to an increase in available capacity to Europe, said Thomson.
Air Canada routes all of its India flights through London.

"We have been and continue to be off-budget there, and I don't see that strengthening up," said Thomson of India. The airline has cut New Delhi capacity for the winter by substituting all-passenger 747s for some flying by B-747 combis. -Air Cargo Newsroom Tel +44 171 542 7706 Fax +44 171 542 5017
